newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said there would be no news conference after today's Commission meeting but that he would be available to reporters from 1700/1500 GMT.

Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan briefed on the Social Affairs Council. She said the Commission expected a common position on the burden of proof in discrimination cases. The Commission is pleased to see the end of the tunnel on this issue but disappointed that the common position will not include social security areas, Nolan said.

Spokesman Jochen Kubosch briefed on the Telecoms Council. He said the Council would probably adopt a Commission communication on satellite communications and a resolution on numbering. Kubosch said other discussions would focus on the telecoms sector liberalisation, mobile and wireless telephony, the World Radiocommunication Conference and a report on the fight against illegal and prejudicial contents on the Internet.
Kubosch also briefed on the Court of Justice judgments.
In answer to a question, van der Pas said there would be a news conference at 1230/1030 GMT on June 27 in Amsterdam during the meeting between the Commission, the Dutch Presidency and EU candidates.

Van der Pas also stressed the commitment made at the European Council in Amsterdam to take the decisions on institutional questions left open at the summit before any new accession to the EU. One of these questions, said van der Pas, is how to compensate large member states when the number of their Commissioners will be cut from two to one.
Van der Pas said negotitations on institutional issues would not involve countries that are not part of the Union.
Van der Pas said the concept of flexibility, as extended in Amsterdam had different meanings when speaking about first pillar or second pillar issues.
Van der Pas said he hoped that the text of the inter-governmental conference (IGC), as finalised by the ambassadors and officials, would be available in the next few days.
Van der Pas said the IGC had been officially closed in Amsterdam and that therefore negotiations with accession candidates could start at the beginning of 1998, six months after the summit.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/572: EU and Australia sign declaration on closer ties.
- Speech/97/146: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer on "The Amsterdam Treaty".
- Speech/97/147: Speech by Commissioner Emma Bonino on "Fish and aquaculture processing: strategy and stakes.
